newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore police seize heroin, arrest 14 in raids.
newsitem.headline: Singapore police seize heroin, arrest 14 in raids.

text.p: Singapore police smashed a drugs syndicate on Saturday, arresting 14 people and seizing 8.3 kg (18.5 pounds) of heroin, state television said.
Four of those captured by officers of the Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB), who were acting on a tip-off, were major players on the Singapore drugs scene, it said.
Twelve Singaporeans, one Malaysian and a Thai were arrested in the operation which flushed out two separate drugs hideouts. Fifteen opium pellets were also seized.
No details of the value of the haul were given.

Singapore has tough anti-drug laws including a mandatory death sentence for anyone aged over 18 years found guilty of trafficking more than 15 grams (half an ounce) of heroin, 30 grams (an ounce) of morphine or 500 grams (18 ounces) of cannabis.
Of the nearly 280 people hanged for various crimes in Singapore since 1975, over half have been for drug-related offences.
